standard.title: Technical and academic vocabulary for precision
standard.description: use an expanded technical and academic vocabulary for precision when writing academic texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse how vocabulary choices contribute to style, mood and tone (AC9E9LA08). They have not yet applied an expanded technical and academic vocabulary for precision when writing academic texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use an expanded technical and academic vocabulary for precision when writing academic texts.

nodes.label: Recognising technical and academic vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the meaning of an increasing range of technical and academic vocabulary relevant to literary and textual analysis.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the meaning of at least two technical vocabulary terms relevant to literary analysis (e.g. ‘iambic pentameter’, ‘alliteration’) in context.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain the meaning of a range of technical and academic vocabulary across literary, grammatical and rhetorical analysis, including terms specific to poetry, prose and multimodal texts.
wider: Compare technical vocabulary across different analytical disciplines (e.g. film analysis vocabulary versus literary criticism vocabulary) to examine how field-specific terminology shapes what can be said
Examine how academic vocabulary is used differently in student writing versus published criticism — identifying where precision is achieved or where general language replaces precision
Analyse how First Nations Australian scholars and critics have developed or reclaimed technical vocabulary for analysing their own literary and cultural traditions
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to use technical vocabulary with precision in their own writing — a capability that depends on first having a working recognition-level understanding of those terms. Students who cannot identify terms accurately cannot deploy them precisely.

response_modes.reason: Technical vocabulary for literary and textual analysis must be accumulated across text encounters — students need to build a working repertoire of terms that they can deploy in novel analytical contexts.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies the meaning of at least two technical or academic vocabulary terms in context
Can explain how the terms are used to describe specific textual features

nodes.label: Using technical vocabulary for precision in academic writing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use an expanded technical and academic vocabulary with precision in their own academic writing, selecting terms that accurately describe textual features and effects.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two technical or academic vocabulary terms accurately and precisely in a short piece of analytical writing about a text.
nodes.typical_width: Produce academic writing that consistently uses technical vocabulary to describe textual features (structural, grammatical, literary) with precision, selecting terms that are more accurate than everyday language would allow.
wider: Write analysis of a poetry text using specific prosodic terminology (iambic pentameter, caesura, enjambment) with precision, evaluating how accurate vocabulary enables more exact analysis
Compare own analytical writing before and after deliberately expanding technical vocabulary, examining where vocabulary precision strengthens argument
Write analytical response on a First Nations Australian text using both standard literary critical vocabulary and any specific terminology from First Nations critical traditions

response_modes.reason: Using technical vocabulary with genuine precision — not just inserting terms — requires practice across writing tasks; students commonly recognise terms but deploy them inaccurately or superficially in their own writing.

success_criteria: Uses at least two technical vocabulary terms accurately in own analytical writing
Demonstrates that the technical term is more precise than everyday language would be in the same context
